deep-learning.title: Neural Network Architecture
deep-learning.description: The structural design of interconnected layers of artificial neurons.
deep-learning.tldr: Neural networks consist of layers of interconnected nodes organized in input, hidden, and output layers. Each connection has a learnable weight. Networks learn by forward propagation and backpropagation.

whyItMatters.title: Image Recognition
whyItMatters.text: CNNs power facial recognition, medical imaging, and autonomous vehicles.

whyItMatters.title: NLP
whyItMatters.text: Transformers power ChatGPT, Google Translate, and sentiment analysis.

whyItMatters.title: Autonomous Systems
whyItMatters.text: Self-driving cars use multi-modal neural networks.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Neural networks are inspired by biological neurons. Each neuron receives inputs, multiplies by weights, sums them, adds bias, and applies an activation function. A single neuron learns only linear relationships. Stacking layers enables learning increasingly abstract features: first edges, then textures, then shapes, then objects. Training uses backpropagation: compute loss, calculate gradients, update weights opposite to gradient.

pitfalls.text: Adding more layers always improves performance. Deeper networks can degrade due to vanishing gradients.
Neural networks are black boxes. SHAP and Grad-CAM provide interpretability.
More neurons always means better learning. Excessive capacity leads to overfitting.
All neural networks need GPU. Small networks train fine on CPU.

deep-learning.title: Transformers
deep-learning.description: Architecture using self-attention to process sequential data in parallel.
deep-learning.tldr: Transformers use self-attention to process all tokens simultaneously, enabling parallel training and long-range dependencies. They replaced RNNs as the dominant architecture for NLP and are now used in vision, audio, and multi-modal tasks.

whyItMatters.title: Large Language Models
whyItMatters.text: GPT-4, Claude, and Gemini are transformer-based.

whyItMatters.title: Computer Vision
whyItMatters.text: Vision Transformers achieve state-of-the-art image classification.

whyItMatters.title: Protein Folding
whyItMatters.text: AlphaFold2 predicts 3D protein structures using transformers.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Self-attention computes relevance scores between all token pairs through Q,K,V matrices. Attention(Q,K,V)=softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))*V. Unlike RNNs which process sequentially, transformers process all tokens in parallel. Multi-head attention runs multiple operations in parallel. Positional encodings give tokens position information since the architecture is permutation-invariant.

pitfalls.text: O(n^2) memory limits context window size.
Attention weights are not importance scores.
RNNs can be more efficient for simple sequential patterns.
Massive data needed for pre-training; fine-tuning works with less.

keyTerms.definition: Each token computes relevance with all other tokens.
Multiple attention operations in parallel with different projections.
Adds position information to token embeddings.
Prevents tokens from attending to future tokens in decoder-only models.

codeExamples.title: Self-Attention from Scratch
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np

def self_attention(X, dk):
    Q = X @ np.random.randn(X.shape[1], dk) * 0.1
    K = X @ np.random.randn(X.shape[1], dk) * 0.1
    V = X @ np.random.randn(X.shape[1], dk) * 0.1
    scores = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(dk)
    w = np.exp(scores) / np.exp(scores).sum(-1, keepdims=True)
    return w @ V

X = np.random.randn(4, 8)
print('Output shape:', self_attention(X, 4).shape)

deep-learning.title: Backpropagation
deep-learning.description: The algorithm computing gradients through the network using the chain rule.
deep-learning.tldr: Backpropagation efficiently computes the gradient of the loss with respect to every weight by applying the chain rule backwards from output to input, enabling weight updates via gradient descent.

whyItMatters.title: Every Neural Network
whyItMatters.text: All neural networks use backpropagation for training.

whyItMatters.title: Automatic Differentiation
whyItMatters.text: PyTorch and TensorFlow implement it automatically via autograd.

whyItMatters.title: Scientific Computing
whyItMatters.text: Physics-informed neural networks use it to solve differential equations.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Imagine a factory assembly line. If the final product is defective, backpropagation traces the error backwards through each station, computing how much each weight contributed. It applies the chain rule: dL/dw = dL/da * da/dz * dz/dw. The backward pass computes all partial derivatives efficiently in one sweep, reusing intermediate computations for O(n) complexity.

pitfalls.text: Can get stuck in local minima; high-dimensional surfaces have saddle points.
Vanishing gradients prevent deep network training; solved by ReLU and residual connections.
Requires differentiable functions; non-differentiable ops break gradient flow.
Only used during training; inference is just a forward pass.

keyTerms.definition: Vector of partial derivatives pointing in direction of steepest increase.
Computing output by passing input through each layer.
Updates weights by moving opposite to gradient, scaled by learning rate.

codeExamples.title: Backpropagation Manually
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np
np.random.seed(42)
X = np.random.randn(100, 1)
y = 2 * X + 1 + np.random.randn(100, 1) * 0.1

W1 = np.random.randn(1, 4) * 0.1
W2 = np.random.randn(4, 1) * 0.1
lr = 0.01

for i in range(1000):
    h = np.maximum(0, X @ W1)
    out = h @ W2
    loss = np.mean((out - y)**2)
    dout = 2*(out-y)/100
    dW2 = h.T @ dout
    dh = dout @ W2.T
    dW1 = X.T @ (dh * (X@W1 > 0))
    W2 -= lr*dW2; W1 -= lr*dW1
    if i%200==0: print(f'Step {i}: loss={loss:.4f}')
print(f'Learned: W2={W2.flatten()}')

deep-learning.title: Convolutional Neural Networks
deep-learning.description: Networks using learnable filters to extract spatial features from images.
deep-learning.tldr: CNNs apply learnable filters that detect local patterns (edges, textures, objects). They share weights across spatial locations, making them parameter-efficient and translation-invariant for image tasks.

whyItMatters.title: Medical Imaging
whyItMatters.text: CNNs detect tumors, lesions, and diabetic retinopathy.

deep-learning.howItWorks: A CNN examines images like humans: first detecting edges (layer 1), then textures (layer 2), then shapes (layer 3), then objects (deeper layers). Each convolutional layer applies multiple learnable filters that slide across the input, computing dot products. Pooling layers reduce spatial dimensions, providing translation invariance. After convolutional-pooling blocks, features flatten for classification.

pitfalls.text: Not rotation or scale invariant; augmentation helps but doesn't solve this.
Require large datasets; use transfer learning from pretrained models.
Pooling loses spatial info; modern nets use strided convolutions.
Not best for sequences; use transformers or RNNs for text/time series.

deep-learning.title: Recurrent Neural Networks
deep-learning.description: Networks with recurrent connections that process sequential data via hidden state.
deep-learning.tldr: RNNs process sequences step-by-step, maintaining a hidden state across time steps. While replaced by transformers for most tasks, they remain important for understanding sequence modeling fundamentals.

whyItMatters.title: Speech Recognition
whyItMatters.text: Early speech-to-text used RNNs for frame-by-frame audio processing.

whyItMatters.title: Music Generation
whyItMatters.text: RNNs generate music by learning note and rhythm patterns.

deep-learning.howItWorks: An RNN processes sequences one element at a time: h_t = f(h_{t-1}, x_t). The hidden state carries information from previous steps. Challenges include vanishing gradients over long sequences. LSTMs solve this with cell state and gate mechanisms (forget, input, output gates). GRUs simplify with two gates (reset, update).

pitfalls.text: Vanishing gradients make long-range learning hard.
Sequential processing cannot be parallelized like transformers.
Struggle with sequences longer than ~200 steps.
Teacher forcing creates exposure bias between training and inference.

keyTerms.definition: Vector summarizing all information seen so far in the sequence.
Uses gate mechanisms to control information flow, solving vanishing gradients.
Simplified LSTM with fewer parameters, often comparable performance.
Backpropagation Through Time: training algorithm for RNNs.

deep-learning.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
deep-learning.description: Two networks trained in opposition to generate realistic synthetic data.
deep-learning.tldr: GANs have a generator creating fake data and a discriminator distinguishing real from fake. Through adversarial training, the generator learns to produce increasingly realistic outputs.

whyItMatters.title: Image Generation
whyItMatters.text: StyleGAN generates photorealistic faces that don't exist.

whyItMatters.title: Data Augmentation
whyItMatters.text: Medical researchers generate synthetic X-rays for rare conditions.

whyItMatters.title: Super Resolution
whyItMatters.text: SRGAN enhances low-resolution images to high-resolution.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Imagine an art forger (generator) and critic (discriminator) in an arms race. The forger creates paintings to fool the critic while the critic learns to spot fakes. Minimax game: min_G max_D E[log D(x)] + E[log(1-D(G(z)))]. Generator improves by fooling discriminator. Training is unstable; mode collapse is common.

pitfalls.text: Training is notoriously unstable; mode collapse is common.
No single metric for quality; FID and IS are proxies.
Require large datasets and significant compute.
Diffusion models are replacing GANs for many tasks.

keyTerms.definition: Creates synthetic data from random noise.
Classifies inputs as real or generated.
Generator produces limited variety of outputs.
Frchet Inception Distance: measures quality of generated images.

codeExamples.title: Simple GAN
codeExamples.code:
import torch, torch.nn as nn

class G(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1,32), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(32,1))
    def forward(self, z): return self.net(z)

class D(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1,32), nn.LeakyReLU(0.2), nn.Linear(32,1), nn.Sigmoid())
    def forward(self, x): return self.net(x)

g, d = G(), D()
opt_g = torch.optim.Adam(g.parameters(), lr=0.001)
opt_d = torch.optim.Adam(d.parameters(), lr=0.001)
crit = nn.BCELoss()
real = torch.randn(100, 1) + 2

for i in range(500):
    z = torch.randn(100, 1)
    fake = g(z).detach()
    d_loss = crit(d(real), torch.ones(100,1)) + crit(d(fake), torch.zeros(100,1))
    opt_d.zero_grad(); d_loss.backward(); opt_d.step()
    g_loss = crit(d(g(torch.randn(100,1))), torch.ones(100,1))
    opt_g.zero_grad(); g_loss.backward(); opt_g.step()
print('Generated:', g(torch.randn(5,1)).detach().flatten().round().tolist())

deep-learning.title: Transfer Learning
deep-learning.description: Reusing a pretrained model on a new task with less data.
deep-learning.tldr: Transfer learning takes a model pretrained on a large dataset and fine-tunes it for a specific task. This reduces training time and data requirements while often achieving better performance than training from scratch.

whyItMatters.title: Medical Imaging
whyItMatters.text: Models pretrained on ImageNet fine-tuned for X-ray analysis.

whyItMatters.title: NLP
whyItMatters.text: BERT pretrained on internet text, fine-tuned for sentiment analysis.

whyItMatters.title: Defect Detection
whyItMatters.text: Manufacturers fine-tune vision models for specific product defects.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Like a medical student who studied general anatomy then specializes in cardiology. Generic knowledge transfers directly; only specific knowledge needs learning. Early layers learn generic features (edges, textures) useful for any task. Freeze early layers, train only new layers. Strategies: feature extraction (freeze all, train head) and fine-tuning (unfreeze some, small learning rate).

pitfalls.text: Negative transfer if source/target domains differ greatly.
Fine-tuning can cause catastrophic forgetting of pretrained features.
Domain mismatch requires adaptation techniques.
With <100 samples, feature extraction works best.

keyTerms.definition: Model trained on large dataset serving as starting point.
Continuing training on new task with small learning rate.
Using pretrained model as fixed feature extractor.
Techniques for cross-domain performance transfer.

deep-learning.title: Autoencoders
deep-learning.description: Networks learning compressed representations via encode-decode bottleneck.
deep-learning.tldr: Autoencoders compress input to a latent space and reconstruct it. Used for dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection, denoising, and generative modeling. VAEs extend this for generation.

whyItMatters.title: Anomaly Detection
whyItMatters.text: Train on normal products; anomalies produce high reconstruction error.

whyItMatters.title: Image Denoising
whyItMatters.text: Denoising autoencoders remove noise from medical images.

whyItMatters.title: Drug Discovery
whyItMatters.text: VAEs generate novel molecular structures from latent space.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Encoder compresses input x to latent z: z=enc(x). Decoder reconstructs: x_hat=dec(z). Trained to minimize reconstruction error. The bottleneck forces learning compressed representations. VAEs add probabilistic structure: encoder outputs mean and variance, z is sampled from distribution, making latent space continuous for generation.

pitfalls.text: Can learn identity function if latent space is too large.
VAEs produce blurry images compared to GANs.
Latent space may not be meaningful without proper regularization.
Not as good for generation as modern diffusion models.

keyTerms.definition: Maps input to compressed latent representation.
Reconstructs input from latent representation.
Compressed representation space capturing important features.
Variational Autoencoder: learns probabilistic latent space for generation.

codeExamples.title: Autoencoder for Anomaly Detection
codeExamples.code:
import torch, torch.nn as nn

class AE(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.enc = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(20,16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16,4))
        self.dec = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4,16), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(16,20))
    def forward(self, x): return self.dec(self.enc(x))

normal = torch.randn(500, 20) * 0.5
anomaly = torch.randn(50, 20) * 2 + 5
model = AE()
opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)

for i in range(200):
    loss = nn.MSELoss()(model(normal), normal)
    opt.zero_grad(); loss.backward(); opt.step()

with torch.no_grad():
    ne = nn.MSELoss(reduction='none')(model(normal), normal).mean(1)
    ae = nn.MSELoss(reduction='none')(model(anomaly), anomaly).mean(1)
    print(f'Normal err: {ne.mean():.4f}, Anomaly err: {ae.mean():.4f}')

deep-learning.title: Batch Normalization
deep-learning.description: Normalizing layer inputs to stabilize and accelerate training.
deep-learning.tldr: BN normalizes activations to zero mean and unit variance per mini-batch. Reduces internal covariate shift, allows higher learning rates, and acts as mild regularization.

whyItMatters.title: Deep Networks
whyItMatters.text: Without BN, networks >10 layers are hard to train.

whyItMatters.title: GAN Training
whyItMatters.text: BN stabilizes GAN training, preventing mode collapse.

whyItMatters.title: NLP
whyItMatters.text: Layer normalization (variant) is critical for transformers.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Internal covariate shift: each layer's input distribution changes as parameters update. BN normalizes inputs per batch, keeping distributions stable. Learnable gamma and beta allow undoing normalization. Benefit: 10-30x higher learning rates, 5-10x faster training. Slight regularization effect from noisy batch statistics.

pitfalls.text: Different behavior during training vs inference; set model.eval() for test.
Not ideal for small batch sizes (<8); use Layer Norm.
Adds computational overhead for running statistics.
Less effective for recurrent networks; use Layer Norm.

keyTerms.definition: Change in input distributions during training.
Moving averages of batch means/variances for inference.
Normalizes across features instead of across batch.

import torch, torch.nn as nn

plain = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(100,256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(256,256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(256,10))
bn_net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(100,256), nn.BatchNorm1d(256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(256,256), nn.BatchNorm1d(256), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(256,10))

    print(f'{name}: acc={acc:.3f}')

deep-learning.title: Dropout Regularization
deep-learning.description: Randomly deactivating neurons during training to prevent co-adaptation.
deep-learning.tldr: Dropout randomly sets a fraction of neurons to zero during each training step. Prevents neurons from co-adapting and acts as an implicit ensemble of sub-networks.

whyItMatters.title: LLMs
whyItMatters.text: GPT and BERT use dropout throughout their architectures.

whyItMatters.title: Image Classification
whyItMatters.text: Dropout in FC layers of CNNs prevents overfitting.

whyItMatters.title: Medical Diagnosis
whyItMatters.text: Dropout provides more calibrated uncertainty estimates.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Like a teacher randomly removing students each day, forcing remaining students to work independently. Each neuron kept with probability p. During inference, all neurons kept but scaled by p. Equivalent to averaging exponential number of sub-networks, reducing variance and improving generalization.

pitfalls.text: Only during training, not inference; use model.eval().
High rates (>0.5) can prevent learning; use 0.1-0.3.
Less effective for convolutional layers; use SpatialDropout2D.
Adds training noise which can slow convergence.

deep-learning.title: Residual Connections
deep-learning.description: Skip connections adding input directly to output, enabling very deep networks.
deep-learning.tldr: Residual connections: y = F(x) + x. Allows gradients to flow directly, solving degradation problem. ResNets enabled 150+ layer networks.

whyItMatters.title: Deep Vision
whyItMatters.text: ResNet-152 achieves 3.57% top-5 error on ImageNet.

whyItMatters.title: Transformers
whyItMatters.text: Every transformer block uses residual connections.

whyItMatters.title: U-Net
whyItMatters.text: Skip connections between encoder and decoder for segmentation.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Without skip connections, deeper networks often perform worse. ResNets make it easy: blocks only learn residuals F(x)=H(x)-x. If optimal is identity, F(x) learns zero. Skip connections create gradient highways preventing vanishing gradients in very deep networks.

pitfalls.text: Add memory overhead; input must be stored until skip connection.
Minimal benefit for shallow networks (<10 layers).
Dimension changes require 1x1 convolution in skip path.
Can mask layer failure; if a layer learns nothing, skip carries signal.

keyTerms.definition: Shortcut adding input directly to output.
Adding layers increases training error; residuals solve this.
Skip connection where input is added directly.

codeExamples.title: Residual Block
codeExamples.code:
import torch, torch.nn as nn

class ResBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.block = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(dim,dim), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(dim,dim))
    def forward(self, x): return torch.relu(self.block(x) + x)  # Skip!

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(10,64), *[ResBlock(64) for _ in range(5)], nn.Linear(64,2))
x = torch.randn(32, 10)
print(f'Output: {model(x).shape}, With skip connections for gradient flow')

deep-learning.title: Attention Mechanism
deep-learning.description: Dynamic focus on relevant input parts when producing each output.
deep-learning.tldr: Attention computes weighted sums of input elements based on learned relevance. Core mechanism behind transformers, enabling long-range dependency capture.

whyItMatters.title: Translation
whyItMatters.text: Decoder focuses on relevant source words when translating.

whyItMatters.title: Visual QA
whyItMatters.text: Models focus on specific image regions when answering questions.

whyItMatters.title: Speech
whyItMatters.text: Attention aligns audio frames with text tokens.

deep-learning.howItWorks: When processing output element, which inputs matter? (1) Compute attention scores between queries and keys. (2) Apply softmax for weights summing to 1. (3) Weighted sum of values. Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))*V. Multi-head attention runs this with multiple projections simultaneously.

pitfalls.text: O(n^2) in sequence length; expensive for long sequences.
Not all attention weights are meaningful; some are regularization.
Cross-attention attends between two different sequences.
Causal masking prevents attending to future tokens.

Attention between two different sequences.

codeExamples.title: Multi-Head Attention
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np

class MHA:
    def __init__(self, dm=8, nh=2):
        self.dk, self.nh = dm//nh, nh
        self.Wq = np.random.randn(dm,dm)*0.1
        self.Wk = np.random.randn(dm,dm)*0.1
        self.Wv = np.random.randn(dm,dm)*0.1
    def forward(self, x):
        Q, K, V = x@self.Wq, x@self.Wk, x@self.Wv
        n = len(x)
        Q = Q.reshape(n,self.nh,self.dk).transpose(1,0,2)
        K = K.reshape(n,self.nh,self.dk).transpose(1,0,2)
        V = V.reshape(n,self.nh,self.dk).transpose(1,0,2)
        outs = []
        for h in range(self.nh):
            s = Q[h]@K[h].T/np.sqrt(self.dk)
            w = np.exp(s)/np.exp(s).sum(-1,keepdims=True)
            outs.append(w@V[h])
        return np.concatenate(outs, -1)

print(MHA().forward(np.random.randn(5,8)).shape)

deep-learning.title: Optimizers
deep-learning.description: Algorithms updating model parameters to minimize loss, beyond basic gradient descent.
deep-learning.tldr: Optimizers determine how weights are updated. Adaptive optimizers like Adam adjust learning rates per-parameter based on historical gradient statistics, leading to faster convergence.

codeExamples.title: Optimizer Comparison
codeExamples.code:
import numpy as np

def rosenbrock_grad(x, y):
    return np.array([-2*(1-x)-400*x*(y-x**2), 200*(y-x**2)])

pos = np.array([-1.0, 1.0])
v = np.zeros(2); s = np.zeros(2)
for t in range(1, 501):
    g = rosenbrock_grad(pos[0], pos[1])
    v = 0.9*v + 0.1*g
    s = 0.999*s + 0.001*g**2
    pos -= 0.01*(v/(1-0.9**t))/(np.sqrt(s/(1-0.999**t))+1e-8)
print(f'Adam converged to: ({pos[0]:.4f}, {pos[1]:.4f}), True: (1.0, 1.0)')

deep-learning.title: Data Augmentation
deep-learning.description: Techniques artificially increasing training data diversity via transformations.
deep-learning.tldr: Data augmentation creates new training examples by applying transformations like rotation, flipping, cropping. Improves generalization and is especially valuable with scarce data.

whyItMatters.title: Medical Imaging
whyItMatters.text: X-rays augmented with rotation, brightness changes, elastic deformations.

whyItMatters.title: Autonomous Driving
whyItMatters.text: Brightness, weather, and geometric variations for diverse conditions.

whyItMatters.title: NLP
whyItMatters.text: Synonym replacement, back-translation, random deletion.

deep-learning.howItWorks: Key insight: a cat is still a cat whether flipped, brightened, or rotated. Training on variations makes the model focus on invariant features. Image: flip, crop, rotate, color jitter, mixup, cutmix. Text: synonym replacement, back-translation. Tabular: SMOTE, Gaussian noise.

pitfalls.text: Augmentations should reflect realistic variations.
Over-augmentation can hurt if labels no longer apply.
Most valuable for small datasets; diminishing returns with massive data.
Test-time augmentation (TTA) averages predictions on augmented inputs.

keyTerms.definition: Blending two images and labels linearly.

import torch, torch.nn as nn

class UNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_ch=3, nc=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.enc1 = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(in_ch,64,3,padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.enc2 = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(64,128,3,padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2)
        self.up = nn.ConvTranspose2d(128,64,2,stride=2)
        self.dec = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(128,64,3,padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.out = nn.Conv2d(64, nc, 1)
    def forward(self, x):
        e1 = self.enc1(x)
        e2 = self.enc2(self.pool(e1))
        d = self.dec(torch.cat([self.up(e2), e1], 1))
        return self.out(d)

m = UNet()

def forward_diffusion(x0, t, betas):
    noise = torch.randn_like(x0)
    a = torch.cumprod(1-betas, 0)[t]
    return torch.sqrt(a)*x0 + torch.sqrt(1-a)*noise, noise

import torch, torch.nn as nn

class ODEFunc(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(dim,32), nn.Tanh(), nn.Linear(32,dim))
    def forward(self, t, h): return self.net(h)

# Simple Euler integration
def euler.solve(f, h0, t_end, dt=0.01):
    h, t = h0, 0.0
    while t < t_end:
        h = h + dt * f(t, h)
        t += dt
    return h

import torch, torch.nn as nn

class MiniGPT(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vs, dm=64, nh=2, nl=2):
        super().__init__()
        self.emb = nn.Embedding(vs, dm)
        self.pos = nn.Embedding(256, dm)
        layer = nn.TransformerDecoderLayer(dm, nh, batch_first=True)
        self.dec = nn.TransformerDecoder(layer, nl)
        self.head = nn.Linear(dm, vs)
    def forward(self, x):
        p = torch.arange(x.size(1), device=x.device).unsqueeze(0)
        x = self.emb(x) + self.pos(p)
        mask = nn.Transformer.generate_square_subsequent_mask(x.size(1))
        return self.head(self.dec(x, torch.zeros(1,1,x.size(-1)), tgt_mask=mask))

import torch.nn as nn, math

class LoRA(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, linear, rank=4, alpha=1.0):
        super().__init__()
        self.orig = linear
        self.orig.weight.requires_grad = False
        d = linear.in_features
        self.A = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(rank,d)/math.sqrt(rank))
        self.B = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(linear.out_features, rank))
        self.scale = alpha / rank
    def forward(self, x): return self.orig(x) + (x@self.A.T@self.B.T)*self.scale

lora = LoRA(nn.Linear(768, 768), rank=8)
trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in lora.parameters() if p.requires_grad)

import numpy as np
from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

def summarize(text, n=2):
    sents = text.split('. ')
    tfidf = TfidfVectorizer().fit_transform(sents)
    sim = cosine_similarity(tfidf)
    scores = np.ones(len(sents))
    for _ in range(30):
        new = np.ones(len(sents))*0.15
        for i in range(len(sents)):
            for j in range(len(sents)):
                if i!=j: new[i] += 0.85*sim[i][j]*scores[j]
        scores = new
    top = sorted(np.argsort(scores)[-n:])
    return '. '.join(sents[i] for i in top)

text = 'ML is a subset of AI. It learns from data. Deep learning uses neural nets. Transformers revolutionized NLP.'
print(summarify(text))

import torch, torch.nn as nn

class EncDec(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, sv, tv, dm=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.enc_emb = nn.Embedding(sv, dm)
        self.dec_emb = nn.Embedding(tv, dm)
        self.enc = nn.GRU(dm, dm, batch_first=True)
        self.dec = nn.GRU(dm, dm, batch_first=True)
        self.out = nn.Linear(dm, tv)
    def forward(self, src, tgt):
        _, h = self.enc(self.enc_emb(src))
        dec_out, _ = self.dec(self.dec_emb(tgt), h)
        return self.out(dec_out)

m = EncDec(5000, 4000)
src = torch.randint(0, 5000, (32, 20))
tgt = torch.randint(0, 4000, (32, 15))
print(f'Output: {m(src, tgt).shape}')
